done.why: I went down into the Royal Puzzle and could not work out its sliding walls or how to get out. I had no map of it and the grid descriptions kept shifting on me. I gave up there with a lot of the map seen but no ending.

about: A Zork-style underground adventure. You are a seeker on a final test set by an old man. The world has a thief on a cliff, a duel with a shadow self, a lake that takes whatever you carry, and a time machine in a museum of the old Empire. It ends in a sliding-wall puzzle.

moments.note: I tied the chest to the rope. The man above took it, and I waited several turns while hearing him count coins before he pulled me up.
Saying hello to the sailor got me a vial.
I dived for the shiny object. A fish swallowed me, and the old man's cell scene followed. My items were scattered but recoverable.
The duel with my hooded double ended with me pulling back its hood. It was my own face.
I pushed the golden machine to the Jewel Room and travelled to 776. The machine vanished, and everything I carried was left behind.
The crown jewels vanish when I take them back through time, so I never found out what they are for.
In the Royal Puzzle the diagrams shifted as walls moved, and I could not map it or find a way out.

wished: A way to get out of the puzzle or to reset it.
To learn what the ring and amulet are for.
To find the old man and reach an ending.
A map or notes to track the puzzle grid.

lines.line: The water has the look of a cold that would open your hands for you, and would not give back what fell out of them
lines.why: A vivid warning that also teaches the rule about leaving things on the shore.

lines.line: You slowly remove the hood from your badly wounded opponent and recoil in horror at the sight of your own face
lines.why: The duel's payoff is a memorable twist.

lines.line: Among the trees, unless you are mistaken, something that is not a tree is keeping very still.
lines.why: Good atmosphere and menace in the cliff scene.

fun.why: The set pieces were good, but the puzzle trap stopped me.

engagement.why: There was plenty to try, and the time machine and the cliff thief drew me in.

difficulty.why: The puzzle was unmappable and had no clear escape.

interestingness.why: The Zork parody setting has many varied scenes and some clever time-travel inventory rules.

prose.why: The prose is witty and atmospheric, especially around the lake, the cliff and the machine descriptions.
